reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: CRM dispute tickets roughly doubled from a Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06). This is not explained by slow ticket handling (median response 1.6d, p90 2.8d, within the 3.0d SLA — E-04) nor by a tariff change (zero logged changes — E-03). The majority of disputed bills (59%, 1,785/3,025) involve ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), which caps how much the confirmed field manual-read completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, 9,200 accounts — E-01) can explain, since that mechanism only produces estimated bills. The best-supported remaining mechanism is a defect in billing import/validation processing of actual meter reads introduced around the same period, producing incorrect bills on actual-read accounts and driving the dispute surge (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: The Aug-Sep 2026 dispute-ticket surge (E-06) is caused by billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which changed the high-consumption check to compare raw register value directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling "none" (E-13); this rule rejects valid actual AMI reads as high-consumption during billing import, forcing estimate substitution for 1,184 accounts (plus 56 with no read received), which together fully account for the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-12) and drive the ticket surge.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
